newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian beet sowing ends, area slightly down yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Russian beet sowing ends, area slightly down yr/yr.

text.p: Russia has nearly completed its beet sowing campaign and the area planted is slightly below last year's 1.1 million hectares, an official at the Rossakhsvyokla sugar beet producers' association said on Monday.
"About one million hectares were sown and we even had areas which planted a bit more than usual," said Alexei Kazartsev.
A government beet output target of 22 million tonnes could be realistic if good weather and sufficient moisture levels prevailed, but it was too early to say whether this would happen, he said.
Academy of Agricultural Sciences agronomist Viktor Shevelukha said he saw the 1997 beet harvest flat on 1996's 16.1 million tonnes due to low fertiliser levels during planting.
Frosts earlier this month across most beet growing areas had, as usual, damaged some cultures, Kazartsev said, but surplus plantings, especially in the Black Earth region, could offset losses.

Russia -- Central and Eastern Europe's second biggest beet producer after Ukraine -- has seen steep declines in beet output from 1995's 19.1 million tonnes and from the annual average for the first half of this decade of 21.7 million tonnes.
Kazartsev said Russia would conduct about 12 beet tests for sugar content beginning July 1 and lasting through the harvest, which ends in the first or second week of October.
Tests would generally run on the first, 10th and 20th of each month, with results available two or three days later.
Up to 60 percent of demand by Russian sugar refineries for feedstock is met by imports of raws, mostly of Cuban origin.
